Met Office issues rain alert for Islamabad, outskirts
ISLAMABAD: The Met Office in a weather alert on Wednesday forecast rainfall in Islamabad and adjoining areas within next two to four hours.
“Rainfall has been expected during next two to four hours in Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Taxila and Wah Cantt,” according to the recent weather report.
Attock, Jhelum, Murree, Galliyat and Gujranwala could also receive more rainfall with thunderstorm.
Heavy rains may submerge low-lying areas and cause flooding in local nullahs and streams, weather department advised people to observe caution in view of the rough weather situation and keep abreast with weather updates.
Water entered in many areas of Rawalpindi on Wednesday morning after heavy rains lashed the city.
Rainwater drains overflowed in Jan Colony, Shalay Valley, People’s Colony, and Raja Ikram Colony. Furthermore, rainwater accumulated on roads in Sadiqabad and Muslim Town.
Many areas, including Fauji Colony and Pir Wadhaye, were submerged after heavy rains lashed the city.
The water level has started to surge in Nala Lai after the rains stopped.
The Managing Director (MD) of the Water and Sanitation Agency (WASA) informed that more than 100 mm of rain had been recorded in the twin cities so far, warning that the intensity of the existing rain system could result in urban flooding.
Heavy rains may cause Urban flooding in low lying areas in Mardan, Swabi, Peshawar, Nowshera, Gujranwala, Gujrat, Sialkot and Lahore, Met Office said. Heavy rains may cause flash flooding in local Nullahs of Kashmir, Murree, Galiyat, Islamabad / Rawalpindi.

- By Sarah Brohi -

Anne Hathaway made every possible effort to bring back Julie Andrews for the upcoming Princess Diaries 3.
In her recent interview with Entertainment Tonight, the Odyssey star revealed that she “did push really hard” on Julie, but she doesn’t feel she should be a part of it. She continued, “First of all, I just want to say if she has a change of heart, we’re down”.
She further mentioned in her statement and noted, “Just anything, really. But we also want to be respectful. Like, for goodness sakes, if anybody has contributed to the world of entertainment and to our collective joy, it’s her. Whatever she wants, we completely understand”. items.title: Economic Cooperation Organization moves to boost regional trade
items.summary: Business leaders call for better connectivity, easier trade and stronger investment links. The post Economic Cooperation Organization moves to boost regional trade appeared first on BOL News.
items.body_text:
ISLAMABAD: A market of more than 500 million people is still trading far below its potential, prompting ECO business leaders and officials to push for faster connectivity, easier trade and stronger private-sector ties across the region.
At a high-level meeting of the ECO Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ECO-CCI), FPCCI President and ECO-CCI President Atif Ikram Sheikh called for practical steps to remove trade barriers, simplify customs procedures and improve business mobility among member countries.
Sheikh said the region’s strategic location and abundant resources provide significant opportunities for trade and investment, but weak connectivity and regulatory hurdles continue to limit intra-regional commerce.
He called for the revival of regional road and rail links, including the ECO Train, as well as stronger business-to-business engagement. He also proposed an ECO-CCI Action Agenda for 2026-27, with specific initiatives assigned to member chambers and mechanisms to monitor progress.
Sheikh urged ECO members to move beyond conventional trade and develop joint production and regional value chains in agriculture and food processing, textiles, minerals, energy, engineering, pharmaceuticals and information technology.
Read More: Iranian business leaders call for new era of economic cooperation with Pakistan
He also called for greater support for small and medium-sized enterprises, women entrepreneurs and tourism, along with regular ECO trade exhibitions and B2B forums to connect businesses across member countries.
ECO Secretary-General Ambassador Asad Majeed Khan said intra-regional trade remains constrained by tariff and non-tariff barriers, customs and logistical bottlenecks, limited business-to-business interaction and payment-related challenges.
Majeed Khan briefed participants on recent ECO initiatives involving trade facilitation, the Economic Cooperation Organization Trade Agreement, customs cooperation, transportation and business mobility.
He emphasized the role of ECO-CCI and national chambers in sharing trade information, creating business linkages and identifying commercial opportunities. He also encouraged the organization of a major ECO Trade Fair or Expo and stronger institutional capacity for ECO-CCI.
Representatives of national chambers from Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyz Republic, Pakistan, Tajikistan, Türkiye, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan shared recommendations for expanding economic cooperation.
They called for regular regional exhibitions, sector-specific B2B meetings, stronger trade and investment promotion, improved transportation and visa facilitation, and closer engagement among business communities.
The meeting focused on turning regional economic potential into measurable trade and investment opportunities through stronger connectivity, practical trade reforms and greater private-sector cooperation.

items.title: World Photography Day 2026 celebrates stories beyond glamour
items.summary: Photography is not just about beauty, it preserves memories, communities and real stories. The post World Photography Day 2026 celebrates stories beyond glamour appeared first on BOL News.
items.body_text:
More than 180 years later, photography has become part of everyday life, allowing people to preserve memories, document reality and tell stories in an instant as the world marks World Photography Day on Aug. 19.
The annual observance celebrates photography as an art, a science and a form of storytelling. It also gives photographers and photography enthusiasts an opportunity to look beyond polished pictures, by capturing real people, emotions, cultures and everyday moments.
The history of modern photography can be traced to 1839, when the French government acquired the patent for the daguerreotype, a process developed by French artist and inventor Louis Daguerre.
The French government presented the invention as a gift to the world, marking an important moment in the development of photography. The daguerreotype became the first practical photographic process and allowed images to be recorded in remarkable detail on silver-coated copper plates.
These plates was then treated with iodine or bromine vapors to make it sensitive to light. It was placed in a camera and exposed for several seconds or minutes. Finally, the image was developed with heated mercury vapor and fixed with sodium thiosulfate or salt water.
But taking a photograph at the time was nothing like taking one today. Photography was therefore a specialized and time consuming activity, far removed from the instant images people now capture every day.
Photography gradually became easier to use as technology improved, because In the 1880s, George Eastman played a major role in making photography more accessible by developing dry photographic film. Unlike the heavy metal plates used in earlier processes, the new film was easier to carry and handle.
Eastman took another major step in 1888, when he introduced the Kodak camera. The camera helped move photography beyond professional studios and specialists, giving more ordinary people the opportunity to record family occasions, travels and everyday life.
From there, photography continued to evolve through improvements in film, cameras and color images, eventually leading to the digital technology that dominates the modern era.
Today, a camera is often no farther away than a person’s pocket. Digital cameras and smartphones have made it possible to take, edit and share photographs within seconds. A person no longer needs expensive equipment or knowledge of photographic chemicals to capture an important moment.
A busy street, a local market, a hardworking parent, an elderly neighbor, a child’s smile or even a quiet moment at home can become a photograph that tells a story.
Social media has taken that transformation even further. A photograph taken in one corner of the world can be viewed almost instantly by people thousands of miles away, making photography an important part of how people experience and understand different communities and cultures.
World Photography Day is observed every year on Aug. 19, a date closely linked to the history of photography and the 1839 announcement of the daguerreotype process.
The first official World Photography Day celebration was held online on Aug. 19, 2010. Nearly 270 photographers reportedly contributed photographs to a global online gallery, which attracted visitors from more than 100 countries.
Since then, the day has grown into an international celebration for professional photographers, enthusiasts and anyone who simply enjoys capturing moments through a camera. While photography is often associated with beauty, fashion and carefully edited social media images, its value goes much deeper.
A photograph can preserve a memory that might otherwise fade. It can document a historic moment, introduce people to unfamiliar cultures, highlight social issues or simply show what everyday life looks like through another person’s eyes.
That is why World Photography Day encourages people to move beyond perfectly staged photographs and notice the stories happening around them.

items.title: PM, President salute humanitarian workers on world day

items.body_text:
Zardari honors humanitarian workers
President Zardari praised humanitarian workers and organizations for providing timely assistance to people affected by natural disasters, emergencies and other crises.
He also recognized the contributions of social workers, medical professionals, child protection workers and human rights activists, saying helping people in distress was a collective responsibility.
Zardari said humanitarian workers played a vital role in helping communities respond to emergencies and recover from their effects. He reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to compassion, respect for human dignity and the protection of fundamental rights.
The president also reaffirmed Pakistan’s resolve to work with the international community to advance humanitarian principles and protect fundamental rights under the Constitution and international human rights agreements.
Shehbaz highlights Pakistan’s humanitarian role
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif renewed Pakistan’s commitment to humanitarianism, solidarity and the spirit of service, while paying tribute to individuals, organizations and institutions working to improve the lives of people in need.
He noted that World Humanitarian Day is observed in memory of 22 humanitarian workers killed in the 2003 bombing of the United Nations headquarters in Baghdad. The annual observance recognizes those who continue providing assistance in conflict and disaster-hit areas despite the risks involved.
Shehbaz highlighted Pakistan’s long-standing humanitarian tradition, including its contributions to U.N. peacekeeping missions and assistance during regional and global crises. He also cited the country’s decades-long hosting of millions of Afghan refugees as an example of compassion and international solidarity.
The prime minister said the government was working to protect the rights and dignity of vulnerable and disadvantaged groups while promoting a more inclusive and equal society.
He said the Ministry of Human Rights had taken practical measures through welfare centers, training institutions and protection facilities. Efforts were also underway to improve access to essential civic services for people with disabilities and increase women’s participation in social and economic activities.
Shehbaz stressed that protecting vulnerable groups, promoting gender equality, safeguarding children and empowering young people were essential to advancing human rights, social justice and public welfare.
He said Pakistan would continue to stand with vulnerable communities in both peace and crisis and work to ensure they receive protection, assistance and opportunities to live with dignity.

items.title: Trump pauses 50% tariffs on Canadian goods for three days
items.summary: US President Donald Trump paused the planned rollout of punishing new tariffs on Canadian goods late Tuesday, as both sides indicated they were close to a broader... The post Trump pauses 50% tariffs on Canadian goods for three days appeared first on Iraqi News.
items.body_text:
Trump pauses 50% tariffs on Canadian goods for three days
Washington – US President Donald Trump paused the planned rollout of punishing new tariffs on Canadian goods late Tuesday, as both sides indicated they were close to a broader trade agreement after weeks of talks.
Trump announced the three-day reprieve from 50-percent duties on select goods just hours before a midnight deadline.
The delay was “based on the fact that Canada and the U.S.A., subject to the finalization of documents, have a DEAL!” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney was less definitive, saying “substantial progress has been made” towards a comprehensive trade deal, but “there is important work still to be done.”
Ottawa and Washington have held intense negotiations on revising their existing deal, the United States-Canada-Mexico Agreement (USMCA), which Trump signed and praised during his first term but now says needs to change.
The US Trade Representative’s office said on X that the pact between Washington and Ottawa is set to “include comprehensive market access for all American goods, economic security commitments, digital trade alignment” and other provisions.
A proclamation by Trump to pause the duties added that the suspension came about as “Canada has expressed a commitment to remove the discriminations or unreasonable and unequal impositions at issue.”
Carney said the prospective deal aims to “address outstanding trade issues and deliver greater certainty and real benefits for Canadian businesses, workers, farmers and families.”
– ‘Discriminatory treatment’ –
Trump had signed orders for the 50-percent duties last month, with the White House alleging “discriminatory treatment” by Canada against US alcohol, automobile and dairy products.
The new tariffs would cover products such as wine, hockey sticks and cement.
They target around 5.5 percent of Canada’s exports to the United States, worth about $20 billion, Oxford Economics estimates.
While this only poses a “modest” negative risk to Canada’s economy, Oxford Economics said in a recent report that the duties would “affect central Canada’s manufacturing sector much more severely.”
Canadian negotiators have been in Washington to push for a deal to avoid the new tariffs and also secure relief on Trump’s sector-specific duties — which have battered Canada’s auto, steel, lumber and aluminum industries.
Ottawa reportedly offered concessions like pressuring provinces to put US alcohol and wine back on their shelves.
Without going into details, Trump added in his Truth Social post: “The great Keystone XL Pipeline, long ago killed by Sleepy Joe Biden, may be awoken from the grave!”
Trump has previously called for the revival of the controversial project opposed by environmental activists, which was blocked under his predecessor Biden.
– Political concerns –
“It’s not unusual for a trade negotiation to go right up to the deadline,” former US commerce official Christopher Padilla told AFP.
He expects that the Trump administration threatened new tariffs to try and win early concessions from Canada as the countries negotiate new terms for the USMCA.
Oxford Economics anticipates that manufacturers who stand to be most impacted include those in the cement, paper, printing, wood, clothing and electronic equipment sectors.
With the US Supreme Court striking down many of Trump’s global tariffs earlier this year, the president had tapped an untested legal provision for the new duties targeting Canada.
The US duties will not apply to Canadian energy, potash or goods already facing sector-specific tariffs, but are set to hit products covered by the USMCA.
Trump’s trade envoy Jamieson Greer previously said the tariffs aimed to “hold Canada accountable” for its retaliation against the United States.
Provinces have taken US alcohol products off their shelves, he said, and “given better market access to dairy products from the European Union” among other actions, Greer said in July.

items.title: US, South Korea cut drills short after Trump criticism
items.summary: Annual war games between South Korea and the United States will end around a week earlier than planned, both countries said on Wednesday, after US President Donald Trump ordered the... The post US, South Korea cut drills short after Trump criticism appeared first on Iraqi News.
items.body_text:
US, South Korea cut drills short after Trump criticism
Seoul – Annual war games between South Korea and the United States will end around a week earlier than planned, both countries said on Wednesday, after US President Donald Trump ordered the “inappropriate and hostile” drills scaled back.
Trump said on Sunday that he had told the Pentagon to curtail the annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises — a day before they started — citing his “good relationship” with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.
Pyongyang’s state media criticised the drills on Wednesday as a “most immediate and open threat”, without mentioning Trump’s order.
Hours later, Seoul’s military said the drills would wrap up on Friday, not on August 27 as originally planned.
“We have decided to adjust the UFS exercise period to run from the 17th to the 21st,” South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said in a statement.
The decision was made “at the suggestion of the US side”, it added.
The Pentagon said the “substantially reduced” drills would “preserve essential readiness and… (cause) no degradation to US training objectives”.
The exercises are designed to prepare for a possible attack by North Korea.
They were understood to consist of two phases: the first, focused on defending against potential North Korean threats, was due to run until Friday; and the second, focused on a counteroffensive, from August 24 to 27.
The second phase is now understood to have been scrapped.
A South Korean military official told AFP that Seoul viewed the decision as “unusual”.
Nuclear-armed North Korea has long voiced outrage at the exercises, considering them dress rehearsals for an invasion.
Wednesday’s commentary by the state-run Korean Central News Agency said they pose “the most immediate and open threat” to North Korea and “regional security”.
It did not mention Trump’s order or his desire to resume talks with Kim, with whom he has hinted at being in contact.
Hong Min, a senior researcher at the Korea Institute for National Unification, said Pyongyang had deliberately avoided mentioning Trump.

items.body_text:
Palestinian-American hoists US flag on home besieged by settlers
Qusra – A Palestinian-American has raised the US flag on his home besieged by Israeli settlers, as the United States renewed criticism of the siege that has generated condemnation around the world.
Louai Abu Ridi, who owns one of three houses in Qusra, near Nablus in the occupied West Bank, flew back from his adopted home of Ohio on Monday after settlers trapped residents inside and refused to let in food or other supplies for more than a week.
He was flying the Stars and Stripes outside his home on Tuesday and said he has asked the US embassy to keep raising his case.
“It’s my message to all Americans in the United States to see what’s going on here in the West Bank, how the settlers put us under siege trying to take my own house in the West Bank,” Abu Ridi told AFP reporters inside his home.
Under US pressure, the Israeli military said last week it had given orders to remove the settlers.
Troops took down their tent and detained one Israeli but settlers repeatedly came back by foot or in vehicles.
“The settlers come in freely into my house and they’re not doing anything,” he said of the soldiers.
“They even shake hands with the settlers. It’s like they’re friends.”
– Rare US criticism –
Israeli settlers in the West Bank have been increasingly harassing and assaulting Palestinian residents in recent months, often with an aim to take their property.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing government has pushed to support settlements backed by the Jewish right ahead of close-fought October 27 elections.
US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee, an evangelical pastor who has long supported settlers, has offered rare criticism over the Qusra siege and said he had asked Israel to intervene.
In interviews aired late Tuesday on Israeli television, Huckabee said the United States was committed to defending its own citizens.
“We would like to see severe consequences for people who engage in — and I’ll use the term — terrorist activity,” Huckabee told Channel 13.
“It’s not fair to the families who are Palestinian, who own their homes, who have a right to raise their families without fear,” said Huckabee, who before becoming ambassador had rejected the term Palestinian.
Of the extremist settlers, Huckabee said, “If this little minority, if they think they’re doing their cause a favour, they are making a horrific mistake.”
Around 500,000 Israelis live in the West Bank on settlements considered illegal under international law, amid three million Palestinians. Israel has occupied the West Bank since the 1967 Six-Day War.

items.body_text:
Egypt’s National Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (NTRA) denied rumors circulating about a 35 percent increase in internet and mobile service prices, confirming that no official decision has been issued on the matter.
NTRA spokesperson Mohamed Ibrahim said on Tuesday that the news circulating on the matter is “incorrect so far,” RT reported.
He explained that the NTRA is monitoring the information and rumors circulating regarding telecommunications services and their prices, emphasizing that any price changes will not be approved or announced outside official channels.
Ibrahim stressed that if an official decision is made regarding an increase in internet or mobile service prices, it will be announced through an official statement issued by the NTRA, which will include details of the decision, the percentage of the increase, and its reasons.
The spokesperson emphasized the importance of obtaining information regarding telecommunications service prices from official sources, given the spread of unverified news online.
These statements come at a time when telecommunications and internet service prices are of greater interest to users in Egypt, with rising costs of operating mobile and internet networks and the increasing reliance on digital services in daily life.

‘Staying on Warraq’: Residents formally demand land within New Warraq City redevelopment plan          
        Dozens of Warraq Island residents submitted an official list of demands to authorities on Tuesday concerning their right to remain and be allocated their own land within the state’s development project on the island, several residents who participated told Mada Masr.
The move marked a collective step to demand the government guarantee their right to remain and ensure they have the resources to do so — the latest in a series of efforts residents have undertaken to confront authorities over the nine years since the government sought to evacuate them by force to attract foreign investment to develop the Nile island. Security restrictions have squeezed their resources over the intervening years and led to a deterioration in living conditions.
Top of those demands was a request for land within the redevelopment area to be specifically designated for residents who have chosen to stay to build their own homes. The residents called for a clear timeline for the implementation of the rehousing scheme, with defined mechanisms and fair conditions.
They also demanded the dismissal of all lawsuits filed against the younger residents tied to security incidents that have taken place in response to attempts to remove people from the island.
Residents delivered their written demands in person to a representative of the New Warraq City Development headquarters, where a heavy security deployment was present, across the island and at its entrances, one of the residents in attendance said to Mada Masr on condition of anonymity.
The source said the handover took place without incident, “because we came to demand legitimate rights.”
Mada Masr has reached out to the Housing Ministry’s spokesperson for comment but did not receive a response at the time of writing.
The residents also called for urgent improvements to daily life, pending progress on their main demands, including a primary healthcare unit that provides essential medicines and medical services, the restoration of the youth sports center and postal services, the removal of construction waste and the restoration of affordable sewage pumping services.
They further demanded the organized entry of construction materials and the removal of the security checkpoints at the island’s ferry crossings, saying the measures would help prevent recurring clashes between residents and police.
Clashes between security forces and dozens of residents broke out again on the island this month near the Qolaly ferry crossing, where a security officer assaulted a boy bringing building materials onto the island. The clashes lasted several days, with three protesters arrested and later released.
Amid ongoing tensions over the state’s New Warraq City project and efforts to expropriate land and evict residents, restrictions on bringing construction materials onto the island have intensified in recent months, with materials allowed only in limited quantities and with security approval or otherwise smuggled in.
As confrontations escalated in August, residents held a one-day sit-in at the crossing the government was using to transport construction material, which ended after security authorities promised to organize the entry of construction materials for the residents. The Housing Ministry denied days later that the New Warraq Island Development Authority had permitted the delivery of any construction materials or supplies to enter the island.
Frustrated with the restrictions, Warraq residents launched the “Staying on the land” campaign on Friday, the latest in a series of attempts by residents to organize against the state’s development project and its accompanying expropriations and home evictions, dating back to the formation of the island’s family council in 2017.

                In the daily battle to put bread on the table, buy cooking gas, pay for education and healthcare, the daily battle to provide for the basic necessities of life, the farm laborers of the Wadi al-Mollak village in Sharqiya fight without land, schools, hospitals, roads or transportation fit for humans, without drinking water or a sanitation system, without work that can guarantee subsistence, let alone a “Hayah Karima.”
And yet everyone fights. Men, youth and children are packed every day by the dozens into the dabbaba (tank), as the open-bed pickup truck is known. They set off at the first light of dawn along a deadly road they have no choice but to take. They head to the large farms within the village or in Ismailia, to earn enough to get by and keep fighting.
That is why when their sons come back from the battlefield as lifeless bodies, instead of bringing home the little they had gone out to earn, the tragedy is more than the loss of loved ones. It is an utter defeat that can take years to overcome.
So we saw it on our visit to Ezbet al-Dawoudiya, one of dozens of similar ezbas in Wadi al-Mollak.
We arrived on Thursday. Two days earlier, a dabbaba carrying some of Dawoudiya’s residents to work at mango farms belonging to the Armed Forces’ National Service Projects Organizations in the Abu Sultan area of Ismailia collided with another coming from the opposite direction from the Bahr al-Baqar village, carrying boys and girls to other farms in the same area. The collision killed 19 people, including one person from Dawoudiya whom the residents tell us succumbed to his injuries on Saturday. Twenty nine more people were injured in the crash.
In total, 12 of the village’s young men and children were killed and six others injured, some critically.
***
“We want to go to the funeral,” we tell the driver of the dabbaba, the only way to get to the ezbas of the village.
“Which funeral?” he asks. “The one in Abu Ghazbawy, Abu Agwa or Shelh? There’s one or two dead in each. The group funeral was Wednesday. The governor came and all the big shots.”
Following the advice of the women sitting beside us in the truck, we decide to go to Dawoudiya, the ezba with the largest number of victims: eight killed and six injured, residents would tell us later.
The truck sets off along a partly paved road no more than four meters wide, running between two canals. There were no street lights. Every time we hit a bump or a pothole, we grip the truck’s metal rails tighter.
Day laborers in Wadi al-Mollak do not only work in the mango harvest during the summer. Throughout the year, they also pick fruit in the large citrus farms surrounding them, or they sort and pack produce at export stations in Beheira and Alexandria, village residents will tell us later. The workers are taken to those farms and stations in the same open pick-ups they use to reach the mango farms.
Most of the land in Wadi al-Mollak once belonged to Arabia for Land Reclamation, established in the 1960s. The farm laborers called it the “Yugoslav company” because it brought in experts and equipment for desert land reclamation from Yugoslavia.
“When I was young, I used to work as a day laborer for the company. I would earn a quarter of a pound,” a man in his seventies from Mollak recalls. “Then, in the 1990s, we woke up one day to find out they had sold large areas of the land to businessmen. We don’t know how. And we’re the people who live here, we didn’t even get a single qirat (175 square meters) of the land.”
On our way to Dawoudiya, we listen to the women’s grievances, which pour out after they learn we are on a reporting assignment.

The Rapid Support Forces and its allies launched a broad offensive across Sudan this week, opening simultaneous attacks on multiple fronts in what military officers described to Mada Masr as an attempt to offset heavy losses on the North Kordofan front and prevent military advances westward.
From an attempt to retake a strategic border area in Darfur to waves of drone strikes across northern and central Sudan that kept the military’s air defenses heavily engaged, the escalation culminated with major gains in Blue Nile.
The RSF and its ally the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North, led by Abdel Aziz al-Hilu, seized Geisan on Tuesday and retook Kurmuk two days later, advancing from SPLM-N-held territory in southern Blue Nile and across the Ethiopian border, three military sources told Mada Masr.
The gains reverse much of the military’s recent progress along the southeastern border, coming only weeks after it recaptured Kurmuk and disrupted the cross-border supply routes that had sustained the allies’ campaign in the region.
As the two sides were fighting in Kurmuk, an RSF force of more than 250 combat vehicles moved on Gabra al-Sheikh, one of the paramilitary group’s main logistics hub in North Kordofan, in an attempt to retake the area it lost in the military’s late-July offensive. The military and allied forces repelled the attack after several hours of fighting.
While the SPLM-N remains occupied on the Blue Nile front, an internal crisis is growing in its South Kordofan stronghold, a crisis that could, a former military source in the movement said, force it to divert forces and resources to protecting its own territory from its own people.
Clashes that broke out last week in Kauda, the movement’s seat of power, between SPLM-N forces and one of its oldest constituencies, the Otoro tribe, were brought under control within days. But this week, the confrontation spread to villages surrounding the town, where clashes and heavy artillery exchanges have driven a new wave of displacement.
SPLM-N has since deployed heavily around Kauda to prevent the fighting from reaching the town again, a buildup that has disrupted people’s daily lives and deepened the strain on communities already exhausted by months of intermittent clashes and tightening security measures, three residents told Mada Masr.
At the root of the latest violence are Otoro demands for greater representation in the movement’s civilian and military institutions — a pushback against what they see as an increasingly centralized mode of governance. Tribal notables in SPLM-N territory warn that without genuine outreach to local communities, the violence will keep recurring, testing the movement’s claim to offer a model of local governance distinct from central state rule and risking a deeper rift between its institutions and the people they govern.
The RSF-led government is facing its own internal fractures. A fourth high-profile defection hit the administrative structures it has built in western Sudan, with Hamad Khalifa, the governor of the Kordofan region in the RSF-led Tasis administration and a member of its presidential council, announcing Wednesday that he is exiting the group.

items.title: Strait of Hormuz to remain closed until US abides by deal, Iranian parliament speaker says
items.summary: The Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until the United States adheres to the terms of an interim agreement, Iranian chief negotiator and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said on Tuesday, directly countering assertions by US President Donald Trump that the waterway is open. In a briefing to parliament, Ghalibaf stated that the strait will […] The post Strait of Hormuz to remain closed until US abides by deal, Iranian parliament speaker says first appeared on Dailynewsegypt.
items.body_text:
The Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until the United States adheres to the terms of an interim agreement, Iranian chief negotiator and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said on Tuesday, directly countering assertions by US President Donald Trump that the waterway is open.
In a briefing to parliament, Ghalibaf stated that the strait will stay shut until Washington complies with the temporary deal’s provisions, including lifting the naval blockade and sanctions, unfreezing Iranian assets, and terminating all military threats and operations.
The Iranian statement followed comments by Trump, who posted on Truth Social that there are no ongoing or scheduled communications or talks with Iran following the formal expiration on Monday of a memorandum of understanding signed on June 17. Trump stated that the US naval blockade “remains fully in place and in effect,” whilst also claiming that the “Strait of Hormuz is open and functioning, and all sea mines have been removed or detonated.”
Shortly before his post, Trump shared an image depicting a map of the strait—located between Iran and Oman at the entrance to the Gulf—circled and labelled “New American Territory.” Asked on Monday about earlier statements regarding plans to declare the waterway US territory, Trump called it a “great idea,” adding, “I mean we control it.”
Trump stated on Monday that the United States is not seeking to extend the memorandum of understanding because Tehran “will not make the deal” Washington considers necessary. Reaffirming that the US holds complete control over the strait via its blockade, Trump acknowledged Iran’s capability to lay ship-threatening mines but described the blockade as highly effective, noting that the US handles millions of barrels of oil weekly, the strait is open, and oil prices are falling.
Addressing Iran’s internal situation, Trump stated that inflation in the country had reached 300 percent, describing Iran as being in a severe crisis and its military as “completely defeated.” He warned that more stringent measures than the current ones could be implemented.

items.title: SouthMed project sales reach EGP 520bn as North Coast drives Egyptian real estate market
items.summary: Talaat Moustafa Group’s (TMG) SouthMed project recorded EGP 118bn in sales since the beginning of 2026, raising its cumulative sales to EGP 520bn since its launch, as the North Coast accounted for 33 percent of total sales among Egypt’s top 10 real estate developers during the first half of the year. The North Coast ranked […] The post SouthMed project sales reach EGP 520bn as North Coast drives Egyptian real estate market first appeared on Dailynewsegypt.
items.body_text:
Talaat Moustafa Group’s (TMG) SouthMed project recorded EGP 118bn in sales since the beginning of 2026, raising its cumulative sales to EGP 520bn since its launch, as the North Coast accounted for 33 percent of total sales among Egypt’s top 10 real estate developers during the first half of the year.
The North Coast ranked as the second-largest sales region in the Egyptian market during the first six months of 2026, trailing East Cairo, which captured 47 percent of sales. West Cairo followed with 11 percent, Ain Sokhna with 7 percent, and international projects accounted for the remaining 2 percent.
The region’s growing market share is driven by its appeal as an integrated coastal destination, rising demand for major projects with prime locations, and a diverse range of real estate products combining residential, tourism, entertainment, and service components.
Leading these sales is the SouthMed project, which benefits from its location near the airport and the inclusion of an international marina, attracting both local and foreign investors. Project data indicates that unit deliveries for Southmed are scheduled to begin in 2028.
The current figures build upon SouthMed initial launch in July 2024, when the development recorded EGP 60bn in sales within its first 12 hours. This figure rose to EGP 200bn in six working days and reached EGP 251bn in less than a month.
Another major development, Palm Hills Developments’ Hacienda Ras El Hekma, also reported strong sales, generating EGP 75bn in its first two weeks up to the end of trading on August 17, 2026.
These figures come amid a shift in the Egyptian real estate market during the first half of 2026. Purchasing decisions have partially moved away from rapid hedging against price increases toward a focus on end-use and long-term returns, favouring projects that offer strong locations, integrated services, product quality, and rapid execution.

items.title: Egypt plans drainage upgrades across 1.4m feddans under new national programme
items.summary: Egypt is preparing to launch a fourth national drainage programme targeting the construction, rehabilitation and replacement of subsurface drainage networks across 1.4 million feddans, Water Resources and Irrigation Minister Hani Sewilam said. Sewilam instructed officials to accelerate preparations for the programme during a meeting reviewing the work of the Egyptian Public Authority for Drainage Projects […] The post Egypt plans drainage upgrades across 1.4m feddans under new national programme
items.body_text:
Egypt is preparing to launch a fourth national drainage programme targeting the construction, rehabilitation and replacement of subsurface drainage networks across 1.4 million feddans, Water Resources and Irrigation Minister Hani Sewilam said.
Sewilam instructed officials to accelerate preparations for the programme during a meeting reviewing the work of the Egyptian Public Authority for Drainage Projects and plans to improve agricultural drainage infrastructure, digital systems and workforce capabilities.
The minister said Egypt was seeking to shift agricultural drainage management from “traditional periodic maintenance” towards predictive digital management and smart response, using integrated digital monitoring and satellite data.
The approach includes digitally coding field drainage networks and using satellite-based monitoring to detect water hyacinth and aquatic weeds, identify areas most likely to be affected and enable earlier intervention.
According to the ministry, Egypt has completed general drainage infrastructure covering around 8.45 million feddans across Upper and Lower Egypt, while subsurface drainage networks have been installed across 6 million feddans. Networks covering another 2.6 million feddans have undergone rehabilitation or replacement.
Maintenance of open agricultural drains has cost approximately EGP 1.5bn over two years, alongside regular cleaning and flushing of subsurface drainage networks and maintenance of bridges crossing agricultural drains.
The authority’s digital transformation plan includes integrating geographic information systems (GIS) with digital databases to monitor canals, drains and pumping stations, as well as using digital applications to track waterways and construction projects.
It is also developing digital asset-management systems covering vehicles, equipment, warehouses, encroachments and land holdings.
Meanwhile, the authority is upgrading its plastic pipe factories and shifting towards polyethylene (PE) pipes instead of PVC for subsurface drainage projects, while installing new production lines and equipment. The ministry said the move could reduce demand for foreign currency while lowering environmental impacts.
Sewilam also called for expanding technical and managerial training to build a new generation of qualified staff capable of supporting the sector’s digital transformation.

items.title: Syria Condemns Israeli Strikes on Idlib Airbase as US Envoy Warns Against Escalation
items.summary: Several regional governments also condemned the strikes. The post Syria Condemns Israeli Strikes on Idlib Airbase as US Envoy Warns Against Escalation first appeared on The Syrian Observer.
items.body_text:
Syria has condemned a series of Israeli air strikes on the Abu al-Duhur military airbase in eastern Idlib province, describing the attack as an unjustified act of aggression and a serious escalation that threatens regional stability.
A Syrian military source said Israeli aircraft carried out eight strikes on the runway of the airbase before dawn on Tuesday, 18 August. The attack caused material damage to the facility but no casualties were reported.
In a statement, the Syrian Foreign Ministry said the strikes constituted a “flagrant violation” of Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and accused Israel of seeking to undermine Damascus’s efforts to stabilise the country and avoid further regional escalation.
The ministry said Israeli attacks on Syrian territory had continued since the fall of Bashar al-Assad’s government on 8 December 2024, despite what it described as the new Syrian authorities’ policy of restraint.
“The continuation of these Israeli attacks, at a time when the Syrian state is exercising restraint and working to consolidate stability and avoid escalation, once again reveals attempts by the Israeli occupation to undermine these efforts and drag the region towards further tension and instability,” the statement said.
Damascus held Israel responsible for the latest escalation and called on the UN Security Council and the wider international community to condemn the strikes and take a firmer position against repeated violations of Syrian sovereignty. It added that Syria would continue to defend its national rights and interests through means permitted under international law.
The attack also drew unusually pointed criticism from Washington. US envoy to Syria Tom Barrack said he was “deeply concerned” by the Israeli strikes and described them as an unnecessary escalation that did not contribute to regional stability.
Barrack said the government of President Ahmed al-Sharaa had not adopted a hostile posture towards Israel and had repeatedly shown a preference for de-escalation. He added that Washington had hosted discussions intended to encourage a diplomatic solution between Syria and Israel and would continue facilitating dialogue between the two sides.
The remarks highlighted growing unease over Israeli military action in Syria at a time when Washington has been encouraging direct contacts between Damascus and Israel.
Several regional governments also condemned the strikes.
Qatar’s Foreign Ministry reaffirmed its support for Syria and said continued Israeli violations of the sovereignty of regional states reflected a dangerous attempt to impose new realities by force. Saudi Arabia denounced what it called a flagrant attack and urged the international community to put an end to Israeli violations of international law.
Jordan called on the international community to compel Israel to halt what it described as illegal and provocative attacks on Syria, while Türkiye said Israel was continuing to target Syrian infrastructure and military capabilities in violation of the country’s territorial integrity.
Egypt also condemned the strikes, warning that continued Israeli attacks on Syrian territory risked undermining stability in both Syria and the wider region.
According to Al Jazeera correspondent Suhaib al-Khalaf, the Israeli aircraft entered Syrian airspace through Lebanon before striking the outskirts of Abu al-Duhur airbase, which lies east of Idlib near the boundary with Aleppo province.
The base was heavily damaged during the Syrian war. Opposition forces captured it from government troops in 2015 after prolonged fighting. Assad’s forces later regained control of the site, but the airport never fully returned to operational service because of the extensive destruction sustained during the conflict.

items.title: Shibani and Grossi Highlight Renewed Damascus–IAEA Cooperation on Peaceful Nuclear Energy
items.summary: Grossi described his visit and meetings in Damascus as a “significant milestone” for security, peace and non-proliferation The post Shibani and Grossi Highlight Renewed Damascus–IAEA Cooperation on Peaceful Nuclear Energy first appeared on The Syrian Observer.
items.body_text:
Syrian Foreign Minister Assaad al-Shibani and International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi announced a new phase of cooperation between Damascus and the agency during a joint press conference Tuesday evening at Tishreen Palace, outlining progress on peaceful nuclear energy and long-standing inspection files.
Shibani said cooperation with the IAEA has continued since “the country’s liberation,” adding that upcoming steps will include expanded technical support from the agency. He stressed that Syria has the full sovereign right to develop a peaceful nuclear program and benefit from its civilian applications, noting that Damascus has adopted “complete transparency” in its dealings with the IAEA.
Addressing the legacy of the former regime’s nuclear activities, Shibani said Syria had voluntarily granted access to the Deir ez-Zor site after more than eighteen years, describing the move as a sovereign initiative aimed at resolving historical concerns. He expressed confidence that Grossi’s forthcoming report would reflect the progress achieved in bilateral cooperation.
The foreign minister also commented on recent Israeli airstrikes on Abu al-Duhur Military Airport in Idlib governorate, as well as ongoing incursions in Daraa and Quneitra. He said repeated Israeli attacks threaten the stability of Syria and the wider region, calling on Israel to halt its operations while reaffirming Damascus’s commitment to diplomatic channels. Shibani added that Syria is working with the IAEA to demonstrate its commitment to regional and international stability, even as Israeli forces “persist in a policy of aggression and chaos.”
Grossi described his visit and meetings in Damascus as a “significant milestone” for security, peace and non-proliferation. He said the agency began working with Syria’s new government eighteen months ago, contrasting its openness with the non-cooperation of the previous authorities. Grossi confirmed that inspectors had been granted access to the previously undisclosed Deir ez-Zor site, enabling the agency to address longstanding questions raised by the international community.
He announced that Syria has “restored its position” as a state in full compliance with its non-proliferation obligations, and said future nuclear applications in the country will focus on energy, healthcare and water management—areas he described as foundations for new international partnerships.
Prior to the press conference, Shibani and Grossi held technical discussions covering recent inspection visits to Deir ez-Zor and another site containing nuclear material discovered by the Syrian government. According to a statement from the Syrian Foreign Ministry on X, both sides reaffirmed the importance of continued coordination to safeguard Syria’s sovereign right to peaceful nuclear energy and to close outstanding files before the IAEA Board of Governors “as expeditiously as possible.”

items.title: Lebanon Approves Extradition of Former Syrian Army General for Trial in Damascus
items.summary: The ruling was issued under the 1951 Lebanese-Syrian Judicial Agreement, after the Lebanese judiciary determined that all legal and procedural requirements for extradition had been met. The post Lebanon Approves Extradition of Former Syrian Army General for Trial in Damascus first appeared on The Syrian Observer.
items.body_text:
Lebanon’s Public Prosecutor, Judge Ahmad Rami Al-Haj, approved on Tuesday, 18 August, the extradition of retired Syrian Major General Adel Issa to Damascus, where he will stand trial for alleged crimes committed on Syrian territory, according to the National News Agency.
The ruling was issued under the 1951 Lebanese-Syrian Judicial Agreement, after the Lebanese judiciary determined that all legal and procedural requirements for extradition had been met. Judge Al-Haj instructed the Central Criminal Investigation Department to transfer Issa from the Palace of Justice in Beirut to the General Directorate of General Security, ahead of his handover to a Syrian security committee at the border.
Issa — the former commander of land forces in Deir ez-Zor and former head of the 17th Division under the previous regime — was detained after visiting the Syrian Embassy in Beirut to complete an administrative procedure. Embassy staff alerted Lebanese judicial and security authorities to his presence, identifying him as a wanted individual with outstanding arrest warrants issued by Damascus and formally requesting his surrender.
During initial questioning, Issa admitted entering Lebanon illegally through smuggling routes, saying he feared prosecution by Syrian internal security forces. Lebanese investigators are examining allegations of his direct involvement in operations targeting protesters and civilians during his tenure in Deir ez-Zor and while commanding the 17th Division.
Issa denied the accusations, claiming his actions were limited to routine military duties. His extradition marks a new step in Damascus’s efforts to hold former military and security officials accountable, as Syria’s new authorities expand cross-border judicial cooperation with neighboring states.

items.summary: Air defense forces shot down 56 drones and two “Banderole” loitering munitions used by Russian invaders to attack Ukraine beginning on the evening of August 18.
items.body_text:
Air defense forces shoot down 56 drones and two Banderole drones launched by Russia against Ukraine overnight
According to Ukrinform, the Ukrainian Air Force reported this on Telegram.
According to military sources, starting at 6:00 p.m. on Tuesday, August 18, the enemy launched an attack using two “Iskander-M” ballistic missiles, 65 Shahed-type strike UAVs (including jet-powered ones), “Gerbera,” ‘Banderole’ loitering munitions, and “Parody”-type decoy drones from the following directions: Kursk, Orel, as well as the temporarily occupied Donetsk and Hvardiyske (in the temporarily occupied Crimea).
The air attack was repelled by the Ukrainian Air Force, anti-aircraft missile forces, electronic warfare units, unmanned systems, and mobile fire groups of the Ukrainian Defense Forces.
According to preliminary data, as of 8:30 a.m. on Wednesday, August 19, air defense forces shot down or neutralized 56 drones and two “Banderole” drones in northern, southern, and eastern Ukraine.
Hits were recorded at 10 locations, and downed targets (debris) were found at three locations.
The attack is ongoing, with several enemy drones in the airspace.
As reported by Ukrinform, on August 18, Russian troops launched a missile strike on Pechenihy in the Kharkiv region, killing 10 people.

items.title: Enemy exerts most pressure in Kostiantynivka sector as nearly 240 engagements reported along front over past 24 hours
items.summary: Over the past 24 hours, on August 18, 239 combat engagements between the Ukrainian Defense Forces and Russian invaders were recorded on the front lines, with the highest number occurring in the Kostiantynivka sector.
items.body_text:
Enemy exerts most pressure in Kostiantynivka sector as nearly 240 engagements reported along front over past 24 hours
According to Ukrinform, this information is contained in a Facebook post by the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine regarding the situation as of 8:00 a.m. on Wednesday, August 19.
The enemy launched one missile strike using two missiles and carried out 87 airstrikes, during which it dropped 302 guided bombs. In addition, Russian invaders deployed 11,130 kamikaze drones and carried out 3,070 shelling attacks, 27 of which involved multiple launch rocket systems.
Artillery shelling targeted the settlements of Korenok, Sopych, Bachivsk, Neskuchne, Bezsalivka, Ulanove, Tovstodubove, Luzhky, Volfyne, Yastrubshchyna, and Seredyna Buda in Sumy region; Tymanovychi, Senkivka, Huta-Studenetska, Yanzhulivka, and Topolia in Chernihiv region. Tovstodubove and Rybtsi were hit by airstrikes.
The Air Force, missile forces, and artillery of the Defense Forces struck nine areas where Russian troops were concentrated, two artillery systems, and one drone launch site.
In the Northern Slobozhanshchyna and Kursk sectors, Ukrainian defenders repelled three enemy assaults. The Russian Federation’s army carried out 54 shelling attacks, two of which involved the use of multiple-launch rocket systems (MLRS), and launched five airstrikes using 14 guided aerial bombs.
In the Southern Slobozhanshchyna direction, Defense Forces units repelled 10 Russian attacks. The invaders attempted to advance near Izbytske, Dovzhanka, Starytsia, Mytrofanivka, Lozova Druha, Radkivka, Bochkove, and Okhrymivka.
In the Kupiansk direction, the Russian Federation’s army launched two offensives toward Novoosynove and Kurylivka.
In the Lyman direction, Russian invaders attacked six times toward the settlements of Lyman and Drobysheve, as well as in the area of the settlements of Ridkodub and Novoselivka.
In the Sloviansk sector, the enemy carried out 16 assaults in the areas of the settlements of Riznykivka, Kryva Luka, and Zakytne, as well as toward Rai-Oleksandrivka and Mykolaivka.
In the Kramatorsk sector, Russian invaders conducted one offensive operation toward Izhevka.
In the Kostiantynivka sector, 31 attacks were recorded. The Russian Armed Forces carried out assaults in the areas around the settlements of Kostiantynivka, Novoselivka, Dovha Balka, Ivanopillia, Illinivka, Sofiivka, and Rusyn Yar, as well as toward the settlements of Vilne, Stepanivka, Novopavlivka, and Kucheriiv Yar.
On the Pokrovsk sector, the enemy carried out 27 attacks. Russian invaders attempted to advance in the areas around the settlements of Udachne, Novooleksandrivka, Molodetske, and Kotlyne, as well as toward the settlements of Bilytske, Novyi Donbas, Shevchenko, Serhiivka, Vasylivka, Myrne, and Hannivka.
In the Oleksandrivka sector, Russian forces carried out three attacks toward the settlements of Nove Zaporizhzhia, Rybne, and Sosnivka.
In the Huliaypole sector, the enemy attacked the positions of Ukrainian defenders 12 times. In particular, they attempted to advance toward the settlements of Rivne, Dobropillia, Zaliznychne, Novoselivka, Lisne, Charivne, and Hirke.
In the Orikhiv sector, Ukrainian defenders repelled one enemy attempt to advance in the Plavni area.
In the Dnipro River sector, the enemy did not conduct any assault operations.
In the Volyn and Polissia sectors, no signs of the Russian Federation forming offensive groups were detected.
As reported by Ukrinform, the total combat losses of Russian troops since the start of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine—from February 24, 2022, to August 19, 2026—amount to approximately 1,471,160 personnel, including 1,190 over the past 24 hours.

items.title: NATO Draws Up 3-Step Plan to Fight Russia if Putin Attacks the Baltics
items.summary: NATO has reportedly developed a three-part strategy for a potential Russian attack on the Baltic states. According to Bild, the plan includes suppressing Russian missile systems, deploying autonomous drones along NATO’s borders and striking key military and logistical targets inside Russia.
items.body_text:
NATO has developed detailed plans for how it would respond if Russia launched an attack on the Baltic states, including a possible invasion of Estonia, Latvia or Lithuania.
According to German newspaper Bild, the plans reportedly form part of NATO’s “Land Warfighting Concept,” which was developed under the leadership of US Army Major Andrew Pingrey. The reported strategy focuses on stopping Russian forces, disrupting their ability to wage war and pushing an invading force back to Russia’s borders.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
As per Bild, the concept outlines three main elements of a potential NATO response.
Striking Russian missiles and air defenses
If Russian forces launched missile and drone attacks against the Baltic states and followed them with a conventional ground invasion, NATO would first seek to suppress the Russian missile threat.
The reported plan calls for fighter jets, missiles and drones to target Russian missile systems. Kaliningrad, the Russian exclave on the Baltic Sea, would be a particular focus because of its concentration of air-defense and missile systems.
Creating an autonomous drone zone
At the same time, NATO would establish an “autonomous zone” along its borders with Russia and Belarus, according to Bild. The zone would serve as a defensive barrier, with drones and unmanned military vehicles operating against advancing Russian forces. NATO troops would not be permanently stationed inside the zone.
If Russian forces continued their advance, unmanned systems would be used to slow or stop them, the report said.
Lavrov Threatens UK With ‘Consequences’ Over Ukraine War
Striking Russian military infrastructure
The third element would involve attacks on targets inside Russia.
According to Bild, NATO special forces could target key military and logistical infrastructure, including airfields, defense factories, bridges and railway lines used to move Russian troops and equipment.
The reported concept also envisages working with Russians opposed to President Vladimir Putin in an effort to disrupt military supplies and weaken further Russian attacks.
Bild additionally reported that NATO plans to establish an “air bridge” through which drones and robotic systems could be transported by aircraft into Russia. These systems could then target military bases and airfields.
NATO’s stated goal: Defend, not conquer
The alliance’s reported concept reads that NATO would not seek to occupy or conquer Russia. Instead, the objective would be to stop an invading Russian force and push it back toward Russia’s borders.
The reported strategy also reflects a broader emphasis on deterrence. According to Bild, NATO military planners do not necessarily want the concept to remain secret, arguing that deterrence works best when Russia knows what it could face if it attacks a NATO member.

items.title: EXPLAINER: 35 Years Ago Today, the World Held Its Breath
items.summary: On this day in 1991, a failed hardline coup in Moscow became the final shock that pushed Ukraine from asserted sovereignty to independence. As Soviet authority faltered, Ukraine’s democratic forces, sovereignty Communists led by Leonid Kravchuk, and public protests in Kyiv, converged against a crumbling empire. Within days, the coup’s collapse cleared the way for parliament to meet on Aug. 24 and declare an independent Ukrainian state.
items.body_text:
Thirty-five years ago, on Aug. 19, 1991, a group of Soviet hardliners sought to turn back the wheel of history. They attempted to stage a coup in Moscow, and for several days, the fate of the Soviet Union, and understandably also of the then still Soviet Ukrainian republic, was uncertain.
Beyond the USSR, the world also nervously awaited the outcome.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
On the eve of the 35th anniversary of Ukraine’s independence reaffirmation, let’s recall these events that precipitated the Soviet Union’s dissolution and the emergence of an independent Ukraine.
Desperate to preserve the Soviet empire
The Communist hardliners sought to halt the democratization process initiated by Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev through his policies of perestroika and glasnost.
In particular, they wanted to preserve the centrally controlled Soviet empire masquerading as a “union” of “sovereign” republics by blocking his plan to preserve this unitary state through a new compromise “Union treaty” with increasingly nationally self-assertive non-Russians.
The Soviet Union was imploding. Within Moscow itself, fractures had opened up. The liberal Communist Boris Yeltsin had broken ranks, adopted a democratic position, and, in challenging Gorbachev, promoted the state sovereignty of the Russian Federation.
When the Russian parliament proclaimed it on June 12, 1990, it became a precedent and opened the door for others. Unexpectedly and unwittingly, Yeltsin served both as the Russian ally and catalyst Ukraine’s pro-independence forces needed.
Fedorov Calls for Wartime Elections, Says Putin Shouldn’t Set the Timeline
Ukraine defends its newly asserted sovereignty
By this time, Ukraine, where Soviet rule had remained harsher than in other non-Russian republics, had also begun to reclaim its rights. Following the example set in the Baltic republics, an alliance of democratic, patriotic forces coalesced in 1989 into the Rukh movement and was promoting an agenda leading to independence.
On July 16, 1990, the Soviet Ukrainian parliament also affirmed the republic’s state sovereignty. Some of its Communist leaders, the so-called “sovereignty Communists” led by Leonid Kravchuk, were now also standing up to Gorbachev, rejecting his proposed Union treaty, and seeking maximum freedom from Moscow.
During the final months of 1990, Ukraine asserted its sovereignty by bypassing Moscow and signing several important agreements and declarations directly with other Soviet republics and neighboring states. In September, October and November of that year, Hungary, Poland and the Russian Federation formally recognized Ukrainian sovereignty. Ukraine also adopted a higher profile at the United Nations and applied for direct representation in the Commission on Security and Cooperation in Europe process.
Another indication of its new independent course came in January 1991 when the presidium of the Ukrainian Supreme Soviet publicly condemned the Soviet military crackdown in defiant Lithuania.
The forgotten first crucial referendum
With Gorbachev stepping up pressure on the republics to sign a new union treaty by announcing an all-union referendum on the future of the USSR, Kravchuk came up with an ingenious compromise: the Ukrainian parliament decided that Ukraine would conduct its opinion poll on the same day as the referendum, a poll that would qualify the terms on which Ukraine would agree to remain part of the Soviet Union.
The three regions of Western Ukraine also decided to add a third question, polling voters on their attitude toward Ukrainian independence.
In the March 17, 1991 vote, 70.5 percent of actual voters (58 percent of those eligible to vote) still supported preserving the Union. But this result was offset by the more enthusiastic endorsement (80.2 percent of those who voted) of the supplementary proposal, which said Ukraine would join only a new “union of sovereign republics.”

items.title: ‘Zero Tolerance’: Polish Woman Charged After Alleged Nationality-Based Attack on Ukrainian Siblings
items.summary: A 46-year-old Polish woman has been charged after allegedly verbally and physically attacking two Ukrainian siblings, aged 14 and 12, in Bydgoszcz. Police say the incident involved nationality-based insults and damage to the children’s toy drone.
items.body_text:
A Polish woman has been charged over an alleged nationality-based attack on two Ukrainian siblings playing in a park in the northern city of Bydgoszcz.
Police received a report that a 14-year-old girl and her 12-year-old brother had been subjected to verbal abuse and physical violence by two adults on Friday afternoon.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
On Tuesday, police detained a 46-year-old woman in connection with the case and charged her with nationality-based insults, violating the bodily integrity of a minor and damaging property.
A 34-year-old man who was with the woman during the alleged attack was also detained. He was questioned as a witness and has not been charged, Poland’s state news agency PAP reported.
The incident comes amid concern over anti-Ukrainian hostility in Poland.
Poland has been one of Kyiv’s staunchest allies since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, but anti-Ukrainian sentiment has also grown in recent years, while the countries’ complex shared history continues to cast a shadow over bilateral relations.
‘Anti-Polish act’
Polish police said the incident occurred while the children were playing with a toy drone.
“The couple most likely did not like the fact that the children were using a toy drone. It was destroyed. They also allegedly made comments about the children’s nationality,” Monika Chlebicz, a spokeswoman for Bydgoszcz regional police, was quoted as saying by Polish broadcaster TVN24.
Russian Strike Halts DTEK Thermal Power Plant
“According to the information we received, they twisted the 12-year-old boy’s arm,” she said, adding that the children did not require medical treatment.
The incident also drew a response from Poland’s Prime Minister Donald Tusk.
“Attacking children is an anti-Polish act,” he said ahead of a cabinet meeting on Tuesday. “As Poles, we have always been very proud of the way we treat our children and children who seek refuge in our country,” he added.
Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński also addressed the incident, saying: “Zero tolerance for hatred, especially hatred directed at children.”
On Sunday, the Ukrainian Consulate General in Gdańsk, a northern Polish port city, said it was monitoring the case and remained in contact with the children’s mother.
“We strongly condemn all manifestations of xenophobia,” it added.

items.title: ЦИАН удвоил чистую прибыль по МСФО за первое полугодие // Чистая прибыль ЦИАН по МСФО составила 2,045 млрд руб. в первом полугодии
items.summary: Чистая прибыль ЦИАН по МСФО составила 2,045 млрд руб. по итогам первых шести месяцев 2026 года. Это вдвое больше аналогичного показателя годом ранее, следует из отчетности компании.
items.body_text:
ЦИАН удвоил чистую прибыль по МСФО за первое полугодие
Чистая прибыль ЦИАН по МСФО составила 2,045 млрд руб. в первом полугодии
Чистая прибыль ЦИАН по МСФО составила 2,045 млрд руб. по итогам первых шести месяцев 2026 года. Это вдвое больше аналогичного показателя годом ранее, следует из отчетности компании.
За второй квартал чистая прибыль ЦИАН выросла на 31,6% — до 1,04 млрд руб. Положительную динамику в компании объяснили ростом операционных доходов и снижением затрат на реструктуризацию. Рост прибыли за первое полугодие обусловлен отсутствием убытка от курсовых разниц (1 млн руб. чистого убытка против 577 млн руб. годом ранее), указано в пресс-релизе.
Выручка ЦИАН в первом полугодии увеличилась на 20,5% — до 8,3 млрд руб. За второй квартал показатель вырос на 22,8% — до 4,4 млрд руб. «Рост выручки превысил динамику рынка недвижимости, как в денежном выражении, так и в количестве сделок»,— рассказали в компании.
Скорректированная EBITDA ЦИАН за полгода достигла 2,7 млрд руб. (+68,2%), рентабельность — 32,7%. По итогам второго квартала показатель увеличился на 60,1% — до 1,4 млрд руб., рентабельность — на 7,3 п. п., до 31,3%.
«Несмотря на сохраняющуюся сложную ситуацию на рынке недвижимости, мы продолжаем активно работать над повышением добавленной стоимости для наших клиентов и улучшением пользовательского опыта на нашей платформе. В фокусе остается повышение эффективности компании за счет раскрытия потенциала операционного рычага и автоматизации»,— прокомментировал результаты гендиректор ЦИАН Дмитрий Григорьев.
В той же отчетности ЦИАН поделился планами по дальнейшей выплате дивидендов. До конца года компания намерена направить на эти цели не менее 30 руб. на акцию. В июне ЦИАН уже выплатил дивиденды за первый квартал в размере 53 руб. на бумагу, включая 23,7 руб. специального дивиденда.
В конце 2025 года генеральный директор МКПАО «Циан» Дмитрий Григорьев анонсировал планы по выплате дивидендов, указывая, что следующий дивиденд компания планирует выплатить в середине 2026 года в размере более 50 рублей на акцию. До этого, по итогам января—сентября 2025 года, прибыль сервиса «Циан» выросла на 23% и составила 2,06 млрд рублей, при этом совокупная выручка увеличилась на 15% до 10,9 млрд рублей. В третьем квартале 2025 года прибыль «Циана» выросла на 45% год к году, достигнув 1,1 млрд рублей, а совокупная выручка увеличилась на 29% до 4,1 млрд рублей.

items.title: Главное на рынке недвижимости к утру 19 августа
items.summary: Компания «Логика молока» приобрела у группы «Автодом» участок площадью 15 га в подмосковном индустриальном парке «Северное Шереметьево». О сделке сообщила сама «Логика молока».
items.body_text:
Главное на рынке недвижимости к утру 19 августа
Компания «Логика молока» приобрела у группы «Автодом» участок площадью 15 га в подмосковном индустриальном парке «Северное Шереметьево». О сделке сообщила сама «Логика молока». Ранее на этих площадях располагался склад автопроизводителя Mercedes-Benz. «Автодом» приобрел российские активы компании в 2023 году. По оценкам экспертов, сумма сделки могла составить от 4 до 5,8 млрд. руб., пишут «Ведомости». На приобретенном участке компания планирует построить новый молочный завод площадью 53 тыс. кв. м. Первые линии компания планирует запустить до конца 2028 года. С запуском завода производственные возможности компании вырастут на 20–25%. Сейчас «Логика молока» владеют 13 заводами.
Логистический оператор BG Logistic арендовал помещения площадью 42 тыс. кв. м в логопарке «NK Парк Валищево» на Симферопольском шоссе (32 км от МКАД), сообщают «Ведомости» со ссылкой на два источника и представителя BG Logistic. По словам одного из собеседников, арендодателем выступает входящая в ГК «Марвел-дистрибуция» фирмы Fplus. По оценкам экспертов, новый склад будет ежегодно обходиться BG Logistic в 336–399 млн руб. Договор аренды закрыли еще в первом квартале 2026 года, но о ней не сообщалось. BG Logistic занимается складской и транспортной логистикой, а также логистическим консалтингом. Владелец — бизнесмен Алексей Веселовзоров.
Банк «Траст» продал на торгах два здания магазинов «Лента» в Москве — площадью 3,3 тыс. кв. м на Перовской улице и площадью 3,4 тыс. кв. м в Беринговом переулке, пишет Telegram-канал «Железобетонный замес». Первый объект купила ООО «Банкротфорум» за 311,7 млн руб. Фирма специализируется на покупке объектов с торгов. Второе здание приобрела ООО «Альтаир» за 359 млн руб. Продажа связана с банкротством компании «Ритейл чейн пропертис лимитед», которую связывают с бывшими акционерами «Траста» Ильей Юровым, Сергеем Беляевым и Николаем Фетисовым. «Альтаир» принадлежит Светлане Сапрыкиной, которая ранее выкупила здание «Ленты» площадью 4,2 тыс. кв. м на Прокатной улице.
«Дом.РФ» снова выставил на торги недостроенный микрорайон «Кузнечики-2» около подмосковного Подольска. При этом начальная цена по сравнению с прошлым аукционом осенью 2025 года была снижена на 44,6% — до 2,63 млрд руб. Площадка примыкает к Варшавскому шоссе. Комплекс включает 11 недостроенных зданий общей площадью более 213 тыс. кв. м на участке 40,6 га. Степень готовности домов, строительство которых остановилось в 2010 году, варьируется от 21% до 63%. Новый собственник сможет достроить существующие дома, снести их либо запустить проект комплексного развития территорий. Потенциал участка позволяет возвести 570 тыс. кв. м недвижимости, включая 358 тыс. кв. м жилья. Вокруг площадки уже сформирована инфраструктура микрорайона «Кузнечики-1», где живут 48 тыс. человек. Аукцион пройдет 18 сентября.
«Дом.РФ» не смог найти покупателя на два участка общей площадью 38,35 га в деревне Поярково в Химках. Это следует из статуса лота на портале организатора торгов. Собственник — девелопер «Стройконцепт». Аукцион должен был пройти сегодня, начальная цена составляла 1,41 млрд руб. На участке можно построить 202,8 тыс. кв. м недвижимости, включая жилье и социальную инфраструктуру, в рамках комплексного развития территорий. Площадка находится в 25 км от МКАД.
В июне 2026 года стало известно, что компания «Логика молока» рассматривает приобретение бывшего логистического центра Mercedes-Benz в Дмитровском районе Подмосковья с целью строительства нового завода молочных продуктов.
Ранее, в январе 2026 года, «Логика молока» приобрела крупнейшую в Сибири фабрику по производству мороженого «Полярис» в Новосибирске, включая холодильно-складской комплекс площадью 35 тыс. кв. м. Компания заявила о планах модернизации и увеличения приобретенных мощностей, а также о намерении инвестировать в расширение производственных мощностей «Поляриса».
До этого, в октябре 2025 года, бывшее российское юрлицо Danone, Health & Nutrition, сменило корпоративное

items.summary: Сотрудники ФСБ задержали четырех граждан России, которых подозревают в организации в Екатеринбурге подпольной лаборатории по аффинажу золота и серебра из вторичного драгосодержащего сырья. items.body_text:
ФСБ раскрыла подпольную лабораторию по аффинажу драгметаллов в Екатеринбурге
Сотрудники ФСБ задержали четырех граждан России, которых подозревают в организации в Екатеринбурге подпольной лаборатории по аффинажу золота и серебра из вторичного драгосодержащего сырья. После производства они направляли товар в Москву для сбыта, сообщили в Центре общественных связей российской спецслужбы.
Из незаконного оборота, по данным ФСБ, изъяли драгоценные металлы в виде аффинированных гранул на сумму не менее 13,3 млн руб., а также свыше 800 кг вторичного драгосодержащего сырья.
В отношении задержанных возбуждено уголовное дело о незаконном обороте янтаря, нефрита или иных полудрагоценных камней, драгоценных металлов, драгоценных камней либо жемчуга (ч. 5 ст. 191 УК). По указанной статье грозит до семи лет лишения свободы. Сейчас проводится розыск лиц, причастных к незаконному обороту драгметаллов и камней, рассказали в ФСБ.

items.title: Спрос на элитное жилье в центре Москвы заметно вырос

items.title: Участок трассы "Таврида" перекрыли из-за обнаружения беспилотника
items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- Участок трассы «Таврида» с 271 по 275 км перекрыт в обе стороны из-за обнаружения БПЛА украинских военных.
- Также временно перекрыта улица Чернореченская и ограничено движение по дороге «Штурмовое-Хмельничное».
СЕВАСТОПОЛЬ, 19 авг - РИА Новости. Участок трассы "Таврида" перекрыт из-за обнаружения там БПЛА украинских военных, сообщил губернатор Севастополя Михаил Развожаев.
«

items.title: В бундестаге призвали применять одинаковые стандарты к экстремизму в Европе
items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- Депутат бундестага Маттиас Мосдорф заявил, что экстремизм нельзя оправдывать геополитической целесообразностью, и Европа должна применять одинаковые стандарты ко всем.
- В 2025 году в ЕС зафиксировали пять терактов и предотвращенных нападений, связанных с праворадикальной идеологией, что больше, чем годом ранее.
- В разных странах Европы действуют правоэкстремистские и неофашистские движения, такие как "Третий путь" в Германии, "CasaPound" в Италии и неонацистское движение в странах Северной Европы.
МОСКВА, 19 авг - РИА Новости. Экстремизм нельзя оправдывать геополитической целесообразностью, у Европы должны быть одинаковые стандарты для всех, заявил депутат бундестага Маттиас Мосдорф. 
По данным полиции ЕС, в 2025 году в объединении зафиксировали пять терактов и предотвращенных нападений, связанных с праворадикальной идеологией. Годом ранее такой эпизод был только один. Число задержанных по подобным делам также выше, чем 10 лет назад. 
"Героизация или политическая реабилитация исторических движений с авторитарными, ультранационалистическими или антисемитскими элементами может усиливать современный экстремизм. Европа должна применять одинаковые стандарты ко всем: экстремизм нельзя оправдывать геополитической целесообразностью", - подчеркнул Мосдорф в беседе с газетой "Известия". 
По его словам важно отличать национальные и патриотические движения от настоящего экстремизм. Само по себе обращение к национальной истории, по его мнению, еще не означает угрозы безопасности. 
На данный момент в Германии действует правоэкстремистская партия "Третий путь", которая активно проводит уличные акции, а в Италии есть неофашистская "CasaPound": ее сторонники нередко выкрикивают лозунги в поддержку Муссолини. Кроме того, в 2025 году организованный ультраправыми марш в Париже собрал около 1 тысячи человек. Встранах Северной Европы же, действует неонацистское движение, оно наиболее активно в Швеции. 
При этом неонацистские группировки не стоит смешивать с парламентскими правыми. Немецкая "Альтернатива для Германии" и французское "Национальное объединение" участвуют в выборах и делают ставку прежде всего на борьбу с нелегальной миграцией, защиту национального суверенитета и критику политики Брюсселя. Однако в европейских СМИ их также часто называют крайне правыми, из-за чего граница между парламентскими силами и радикальными движениями нередко размывается.
